text:
omar: heads-up — since ~02:10 UTC we've been seeing GPU allocs fail in us-west1 because local NVMe eviction backlog is saturating iops. noticed when two large batch jobs kicked and janitor+scrub collided.
ellie: ACK, saw alerts. which nodepool?
omar: nodepool=gpu-preemptible-usw1-a, ~120 nodes affected, eviction queue depth > 4k, %util ~ 99% on nvme. alloc failures show `no available scratch` in provisioner.
jin: ouch. any SMART errors or thermal?
omar: some thermal oscillation on a subset (temp spikes to 78C then fan throttle -> short IOPS drop -> eviction backlog). SMART otherwise ok. here's quick iostat snapshot:
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  await  %util
nvme0n1         1200    18000  96000  720000   12.1  99.3
nvme1n1          900    15000  72000  600000   14.5  97.8
```
ryan: that %util explains it. scrub + janitor both at default concurrency, so they align poorly with peak batch windows.
ellie: can we throttle janitor/scrub or temporarily pause scrub on preemptible pool?
jin: yes — config lives in cluster-ops: `janitor.concurrency` and `scrub.max_ios`. quick mitigation: reduce janitor to 1 and set scrub.max_ios=200 per node, then gradually ramp.
omar: agreed. I'll run a targeted job to reduce concurrency and pause scrub for 15m on the affected pool.
infra-bot: [alert] nvme-high-iops us-west1 (nodepool: gpu-preemptible-usw1-a) — 478 nodes reporting iops > 80% util.
sre-oncall: please tag the incident and link the runbook: https://redwood-internal/ops/runbooks/nvme-iops-surge
ryan: longer term: we should change janitor scheduling to avoid high batch windows (respect gpu job labels) and add a soft-priority for scrub so it yields to provisioning. also consider spreading batch starts over 2 min ramp.
ellie: +1. let's create a short RFC for: (1) janitor priority, (2) scrub backoff during GPU alloc, (3) thermal-aware drain thresholds. I'll draft.
omar: mitigation executed: reduced janitor.concurrency -> 1, scrub.max_ios -> 200; seeing queue depth falling from 4100 -> 600 after ~3m. allocs starting to succeed again.
jin: nice. can you capture the exact commands you ran for the postmortem?
omar: pasted below:
```
# reduce janitor concurrency for the pool
kubectl -n infra patch configmap janitor-config -p '{"data":{"concurrency":"1"}}'
# set per-node scrub limit
kubectl -n infra patch configmap scrub-config -p '{"data":{"max_ios":"200"}}'
# quick pause (ttl 15m)
kubectl -n infra run pause-scrub --image=busybox -- sleep 900
```
ryan: follow-up items: 1) small canary change to janitor scheduler with label-awareness, 2) add eviction queue depth metric to allocator to avoid immediate failover, 3) FYI cost tradeoff — if we keep scrub backoff long-term we'll need more storage ops elsewhere (estimate ~+4% monthly).
ellie: adding issues to triage board. jira: INFRA-3987 (janitor sched), INFRA-3988 (scrub backoff), INFRA-3989 (evict-depth alarm).
sre-oncall: tagging oncall for next 6 hours to watch us-west1 ramp, + paging if queue depth > 3k again.
omar: current state at 02:13 UTC: queue depth 590, iops util 65-78%, allocations resumed, still watching. thanks all. :thumbsup:
